proof_summary: A trial-division factorization and decimal-concatenation computation exhausts all \(n<28749\), showing that each has either at most one prime factor or a nonzero remainder, which excludes every smaller composite. At the endpoint, \(28749=3\cdot7\cdot37^2\) and the factors concatenate to \(373737=13\cdot28749\), establishing the required zero remainder.
